d: Server-agnostic MCP testing framework and full-stack MCP App framework.
x: moonpeak is one npm package with three jobs: An MCP App framework. One file per tool, one folder per View. React hooks for tool data, theme, display modes, state and host actions. The same project runs as a ChatGPT App, a Claude connector and in every other MCP Apps host. An MCP testing framework. Simulations, schema and View checks, Playwright e2e against ChatGPT and Claude style hosts, visual regression and real model evals. It also tests MCP servers written in any language. An MCP App inspector. ChatGPT style and Claude style hosts on localhost, with every host setting in the URL. It is built on the official MCP Apps SDK and the MCP TypeScript SDK v2, so what works in the inspector works in real hosts. Where to start If you want to Read Build your first app Quickstart Understand the folders Project scaffold Write a tool or a View Tools · Views Look up a hook Runtime APIs Test an existing MCP server Any MCP server Ship it Deployment Learn the protocol MCP Apps introduction Try the live demo The starter app runs at https://moonpeak ai.com/mcp . Add it as a custom connector in Claude, as an app in ChatGPT developer mode, or open it in the inspector: For agents Every docs page has a Markdown version add index.md to its URL . llms.txt lists them all and llms full.txt has every page in one file. The repository also ships an agent skill for Claude Code and other coding agents.

d: From npx moonpeak new to a View rendering in Claude.
h: 5. Run it in Claude or ChatGPT
x: 1. Create a project new asks three things: 1. Project name , for example moon app . 2. Resources : which starter Views to include. Pick any of moon , calendar and review , or press Enter for all of them. 3. Install dependencies? Press Enter to install with the package manager you ran it with npm, pnpm, yarn or bun . You can skip the questions: 2. Start the inspector Open http://localhost:3000. The inspector lists your tools, runs the selected one and renders its View in a ChatGPT style host. Switch to the Claude host, dark theme, a phone width or fullscreen from the sidebar. Your MCP server is live at http://localhost:3000/mcp. 3. Change something Edit src/resources/moon/moon.tsx and save: the View updates in place and keeps its state. Edit src/tools/show moon.ts and the next call uses the new code. No restart. 4. Test it 5. Run it in Claude or ChatGPT Put that behind HTTPS see Deployment , then: Claude : Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → https://your domain/mcp ChatGPT : Settings → Apps → enable Developer mode → Create app → https://your domain/mcp Ask "what does the moon look like on Nov 24?" and the moon View renders in the chat. Next Project scaffold : what every folder does Tools and Views Simulations

d: What npx moonpeak new creates, and how moonpeak discovers tools, Views and tests.
x: Discovery rules Folder Rule src/tools/ .ts also .tsx , .js , .jsx , .mts , .mjs Every file is one tool. The file name is the tool name. .test. , .spec. and .d.ts are ignored. src/resources/<name /<name .tsx Every folder is one View, served as ui://<app /<name .html . A <name .css , style.css or styles.css next to it is included. tests/simulations/ .json One file per tool, holding one simulation or an array of them. tests/e2e/ .spec.ts Run by moonpeak test e2e . tests/evals/ .eval.json Run by moonpeak test eval . The app name used in resource URIs is name from moonpeak.config.js , else name from package.json . Scripts Script Runs npm run dev moonpeak dev : inspector + MCP server with hot reload npm test moonpeak test npm run test:e2e moonpeak test e2e npm run typecheck tsc noEmit npm run build moonpeak build npm start moonpeak start Starter resources new can include any of three example Views. Each comes with its tools, simulations, e2e tests and evals, so you can delete the ones you don't need without breaking the others. moon : a detail card calendar : a carousel review : a review and confirm flow

d: moonpeak works without a config file. moonpeak.config.js is there when you need it.
x: Create moonpeak.config.js or .mjs in the project root and export an object: Key Used by Default name resource URIs, server info package.json name, then the folder name version server info package.json version, then 0.0.0 instructions MCP initialize instructions sent to the host none port moonpeak dev 3000, or the next free port vite building Views in dev and moonpeak build moonpeak's own React setup Tailwind or other Vite plugins Then @import "tailwindcss"; in your View's CSS file. Per View settings Settings for one View live next to it, as export const resource = {...} in the View file. See Views .

d: One file in src/tools is one MCP tool: metadata, a zod schema and a handler.
x: Exports Export Required What it is default yes The handler: input, ctx = result . May be async. tool yes Metadata below . schema no Input schema: a zod raw shape { date: z.string } or a zod object any Standard Schema . outputSchema no Output schema, same forms. Hosts can validate structuredContent against it. tool fields Field Meaning description Written for the model: say what the tool does and when to use it. This is what evals test. title Human name shown by hosts. resource Name of a folder in src/resources . Makes this an MCP App tool with a View. Leave it out for a text only tool. visibility "model", "app" default , "model" , or "app" for a helper only your View may call. See Tool visibility . annotations MCP hints: readOnlyHint , destructiveHint , idempotentHint , openWorldHint . invoking , invoked Short status texts ChatGPT shows while the tool runs and after. _meta Extra _meta keys merged into the tool definition. What a handler can return Return Becomes A plain object structuredContent , plus a JSON text copy in content for the model A string One text content block A full CallToolResult { content, structuredContent, isError, _meta } Passed through as is throw new Error "..." isError: true with your message as text See Tool results for how hosts use each part. A text only tool Validation errors Input is validated against schema before your handler runs. A bad call returns a tool error naming the field, which moonpeak test and the inspector both show.

d: One folder in src/resources is one View: a React component the host renders next to the chat.
x: The default export is the View. moonpeak connects it to the host, mounts it and wraps it in an error boundary; you never touch postMessage . Styles A CSS file in the folder named <name .css , style.css or styles.css is imported automatically. Each View is built into one HTML file with its CSS and JS inlined, so it works under strict host CSPs. Style both themes: hosts can switch between light and dark at any time. Resource config export const resource = {...} sets per View options: Field Meaning title , description Shown by hosts and used as ChatGPT's widget description. prefersBorder Ask the host to draw a border around the View. csp.connectDomains Origins the View may fetch from. csp.resourceDomains Origins for images, fonts and scripts. csp.frameDomains , csp.baseUriDomains Origins for nested frames and <base . permissions Ask for camera , microphone , geolocation or clipboardWrite . domain A dedicated origin for the View, when the host supports it. See Security & CSP . Rules of thumb Call every hook before the first early return . Use one useAppState per View for state that should survive reloads. Talk to your server with useCallTool , not fetch , unless you set csp.connectDomains . Keep the View useful in a 320 px wide frame; check it with the inspector's mobile device. Hot reload In moonpeak dev , saving a View hot swaps the component and keeps its state. Saving the resource config or a tool takes effect on the next call without a page reload.

x: Hooks from moonpeak work in every MCP Apps host. Hooks from moonpeak/chatgpt and moonpeak/claude are safe to call anywhere and return empty values outside their host. Tool data Hook Returns useToolData { input, output, content, isPending, isError, isStreaming, isCancelled, tool, result } useToolInput the tool input useToolOutput the structured output useToolResult the raw CallToolResult Host context Hook Returns useTheme "light" \ "dark" useDisplayMode "inline" \ "pip" \ "fullscreen" useRequestDisplayMode a function to request a mode, plus available useHostContext the whole host context useLocale · useTimeZone locale and IANA time zone usePlatform · useDeviceCapabilities web/desktop/mobile , touch and hover useSafeArea · useContainerSize · useMaxHeight layout limits Host Hook Returns useHost { name, version } of the host useHostCapabilities what the host supports useConnection { status, ready, error } useApp the raw MCP Apps SDK App Actions Hook Does useCallTool call a tool on your server through the host useSendMessage post a message as the user useUpdateModelContext tell the model something silently useOpenLink · useDownloadFile · useLog host actions State Hook Does useAppState one state object per View, persisted in ChatGPT, optionally shared with the model useResultState local state that resets on every new result Host extras Hook From useIsChatGPT , useWidgetState , useOpenAiGlobal , useUploadFile , useRequestModal , useUserAgent moonpeak/chatgpt useIsClaude , useClaudeStyles moonpeak/claude Helpers connect is called for you when a View mounts. Call it yourself only if

d: A moonpeak project is a ChatGPT App. What moonpeak adds for ChatGPT, and how to try it.
x: ChatGPT Apps are MCP Apps. Every moonpeak resource carries both the MCP Apps metadata and the older ChatGPT Apps SDK keys, so ChatGPT renders your Views without extra work: moonpeak ChatGPT key tool resource openai/outputTemplate tool invoking , invoked openai/toolInvocation/invoking , .../invoked tool visibility: "app" openai/visibility: "private" and openai/widgetAccessible: true resource description openai/widgetDescription resource prefersBorder openai/widgetPrefersBorder resource csp openai/widgetCSP ChatGPT only hooks They read window.openai and do nothing outside ChatGPT. Prefer the portable hooks when one exists: useAppState already saves to ChatGPT's widget state. Try it in ChatGPT 1. Deploy over HTTPS see Deployment . 2. In ChatGPT: Settings → Apps → enable Developer mode → Create app . 3. Enter https://your domain/mcp and save. 4. In a new chat, ask for something your tool handles. The inspector's ChatGPT host replicates window.openai globals, widget state, display modes , so most issues show up locally first.

d: A moonpeak project is a Claude connector with interactive UI.
x: Claude renders MCP Apps natively. Deploy your server and add it as a connector: 1. Deploy over HTTPS see Deployment . 2. In Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector . 3. Enter https://your domain/mcp . 4. Enable the connector in a chat and ask for something your tool handles. Claude only hooks moonpeak already applies host style variables to the document, so var font sans and friends work in your CSS in every host that sends them. Auth If your server needs a user's credentials, see Authorization .

d: The server moonpeak builds from your tools and Views, and how to use it directly.
x: moonpeak dev and moonpeak start both build an MCP server from your project. You can also use the pieces yourself from moonpeak/server : Export What it does createMcpServer opts An McpServer MCP TypeScript SDK v2 with every tool and ui:// resource registered. createHandler opts A Fetch handler Request = Promise<Response for Workers, Hono, Deno, Bun, Next.js. Stateless: one server per request. createNodeHandler opts A Node req, res handler for http.createServer and Express. resourceUri app, name ui://<app /<name .html RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE text/html;profile=mcp app opts is { name, version?, instructions?, tools, resources } . The easiest way to get it is from a build: or by importing dist/server.mjs and reading the HTML files yourself see Production server . Transport Streamable HTTP at /mcp , stateless. POST carries JSON RPC; the optional GET stream answers 405 because the server never pushes. That is spec compliant and every host handles it.

d: Tool data hook from moonpeak.
x: Everything about the tool call this View was opened for: the input, your handler's structured output, the raw result and its state. Returns Field Type Meaning input In undefined Tool arguments. While the model is still writing them, the partial input. output Out undefined The structuredContent your handler returned. content ContentBlock undefined The result's content blocks text the model sees . isPending boolean No result yet and not cancelled. Show a skeleton. isStreaming boolean The host is still streaming the input. isError boolean The tool returned isError: true your handler threw . isCancelled boolean The user or host cancelled the call. tool { name, title?, description? } Which tool this View belongs to. result CallToolResult undefined The whole result, including _meta . Example Notes Handle isError and isPending before reading output . Call every hook before the first early return . Works in Every MCP Apps host: ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose and the moonpeak inspector. See all hooks in Runtime APIs .

d: Detail card: a date's moon phase, a 7-day strip, and buttons that call the tool again through the host.
x: Part File View src/resources/moon/moon.tsx , moon.css Tools src/tools/show moon.ts with View , src/tools/moon facts.ts text only Tests tests/simulations/show moon.json , moon facts.json , tests/e2e/moon.spec.ts , tests/evals/moon.eval.json What it shows Reading tool data with useToolData and handling pending and error states. Calling the same tool again from the View "Week →" with useCallTool , keeping the new result in useAppState . Posting a follow up question with useSendMessage . d: Review and confirm: the model proposes a stargazing night, the user confirms it in the UI through an app-only tool.
x: Part File View src/resources/review/review.tsx , review.css Tools src/tools/plan night.ts model visible, with View , src/tools/confirm plan.ts app only Tests tests/simulations/plan night.json , confirm plan.json , tests/e2e/review.spec.ts , tests/evals/review.eval.json The pattern 1. The model calls plan night with a date and place. It returns a proposal status: "proposed" with sky darkness and targets, and suggests a darker night when the moon is bright. 2. The View shows the proposal with Confirm plan and Pick another night . 3. Confirm calls confirm plan with useCallTool . That tool has visibility: "app" , so hosts never offer it to the model: only the user's click can confirm. The View then tells the model with useUpdateModelContext . 4. Decline posts a follow up with useSendMessage , asking for the darker night. The decision is kept in useAppState , so a confirmed plan stays confirmed after a reload. Use the same shape for anything the model should propose but the user must approve: bookings, payments, sending email.

d: JSON fixtures for a tool: input, optional mocked output, expectations and host settings.
h: Writing them for an existing server
x: One file per tool in tests/simulations/<tool .json , holding one simulation or an array: Fields Field name Shown in the inspector and test output. In a file with several simulations the id is <tool <slug of name e.g. show moon full moon ; a file with one simulation uses the tool name as its id. tool Which tool; defaults to the file name. prompt What a user might ask. Shown in the inspector's chat. input Tool arguments. output / result Mock the tool result output = structuredContent, result = a whole CallToolResult . The handler is not called, so you can design a View before the backend exists. expect What moonpeak test checks below . host Inspector settings for this scenario: name chatgpt or claude , theme , displayMode inline , pip , fullscreen , device desktop , tablet , mobile , locale . Expectations Key Passes when isError the result's isError matches text the result's text contains the string or every string in an array output partial match against structuredContent Inside output : Matcher Example Matches literal "phase": "Full Moon" equal value object { "week": {...} } listed keys only, extra keys ignored array { "phase": "Full Moon" } element by element, partial "re:..." "re:^MP 0 9A Z {6}$" regular expression " " "ref": " " any value, as long as the key exists $length { "$length": 7 } array length $minLength { "$minLength": 1 } at least that many Writing them for an existing server writes a starter simulation per tool with example input built from its schema plus moonpeak.test.json . Running it again only adds files for new tools.

d: What moonpeak test checks, in about a second, with no browser.
x: Runs your real handlers in process over an in memory MCP transport: 1. Setup : the project has tools. An empty project fails loudly instead of passing. 2. Schema : every tool lists with a valid input schema and output schema if you set one . 3. View : every ui:// resource builds and returns HTML with the MCP Apps MIME type. 4. Simulations : every simulation with expect runs against the handler or its mocked output and is checked. Nothing leaves your machine. Use filter to run one tool or simulation.

d: What MCP Apps are and how a host renders one.
h: What happens on a tool call
x: An MCP App is an MCP tool that comes with a UI. The protocol is the MCP Apps extension to the Model Context Protocol, supported by ChatGPT where they are called ChatGPT Apps , Claude, VS Code, Goose and others. The pieces Piece What it is Tool A normal MCP tool whose definition carries _meta.ui.resourceUri . UI resource An HTML document at a ui:// URI with MIME type text/html;profile=mcp app . View That HTML running in a sandboxed iframe in the host. Bridge A small JSON RPC protocol over postMessage between the View and the host. What happens on a tool call 1. The model calls your tool. The host sees _meta.ui.resourceUri and reads the resource with resources/read . 2. The host renders the HTML in a sandboxed iframe and connects the bridge. 3. The host sends the View its host context theme, display mode, locale, size... and the tool input , then the tool result when your handler returns. 4. The View can call tools, post messages, update model context, open links or ask for another display mode. The host decides whether to allow each request. In moonpeak, steps 1 to 3 are the framework's job. Your View reads the result with useToolData and acts with the action hooks . Why it matters The same server works in every host that supports MCP Apps. You don't build a ChatGPT version and a Claude version: you build one MCP App and test it in both host styles with the inspector .

d: The order in which a View receives data, and what each state means.
x: Stage useConnection .status useToolData Mounted, bridge connecting connecting isPending: true Connected, model still writing arguments ready isStreaming: true , partial input Arguments final, tool running ready input set, isPending: true Result arrived ready output , content , isPending: false Tool threw ready isError: true , message in content User cancelled ready isCancelled: true A View may also be shown again later for an old message for example after a page reload in ChatGPT . Keep anything the user changed in useAppState so it comes back. When a View calls a tool itself with useCallTool , that result comes back as the promise's value. It does not replace the result the View was opened with; store it in state if you render from it.

d: Inline, picture-in-picture and fullscreen, and how to size a View.
x: Mode Where Typical use inline in the message list, as wide as the chat cards, small tables, carousels pip a floating window that stays while the user scrolls timers, players, live status fullscreen covers the chat maps, editors, long lists Read the current mode with useDisplayMode and request a change with useRequestDisplayMode . The host may refuse; available lists the modes it allows. Sizing Height : inline Views grow to their content; moonpeak reports size changes to the host automatically. Respect useMaxHeight and scroll inside the View beyond it. Width : assume anything from 320 px phones to about 760 px. Test with the inspector's mobile device. Safe areas : in fullscreen on phones, pad by useSafeArea .

d: Keeping what the user did in a View across reloads, and sharing it with the model.
x: useAppState holds one object per View instance: Where What happens ChatGPT saved as the message's widget state, restored when the View is shown again Other hosts kept for as long as the View lives { share: true } also sent to the model as context debounced 400 ms , so "the one I picked" makes sense to it Use useResultState for throwaway UI state that should reset when a new result arrives. Anything that must outlive the conversation orders, saved plans belongs on your server: call a tool to save it.

d: Tools only the model can call, only the View can call, or both.
x: visibility Model can call View can call "model", "app" default yes yes "model" yes no "app" no yes moonpeak writes _meta.ui.visibility on the tool, plus openai/visibility: "private" and openai/widgetAccessible: true for ChatGPT, whether or not the tool has a View of its own. Hosts leave app only tools out of the model's tool list, and moonpeak test eval does too. Use app only tools for anything that needs the user's explicit action: confirming, paying, deleting. The review resource is a full example. App only tools are still reachable by anyone who can call your server directly, so check permissions in the handler as you would for any endpoint.

d: What a View can and cannot do, and how to allow more.
x: Hosts render Views in a sandboxed iframe with a strict Content Security Policy. By default a View can run its own inlined JS and CSS which is how moonpeak build ships it and talk to the host over the bridge. It cannot fetch other origins, load remote scripts or open popups on its own. Allowing more moonpeak sends these as MCP Apps _meta.ui.csp / permissions and as ChatGPT's openai/widgetCSP . Ask only for what you use; hosts may review apps that ask for more. Good practice Prefer useCallTool over fetch : the call goes through the host to your server, with no CSP entry and no secrets in the View. Never put API keys in a View. Everything in it is visible to the user. Treat tool input as untrusted: validate with schema , and check permissions in handlers, including app only ones. Use useOpenLink for links so the host can show its own confirmation.

d: content, structuredContent and _meta: who reads what.
x: A CallToolResult has three parts, read by different consumers: Part Read by Put here content the model a short text summary the model can talk about structuredContent the View and the model, in hosts that pass it the data the View renders _meta the View only data the model should not see ids, large payloads, signed URLs When your handler returns a plain object, moonpeak puts it in structuredContent and a JSON copy in content . For large data, return the shape yourself so the model gets a summary: Throwing returns isError: true with your message as text. The View sees isError in useToolData ; useCallTool throws it as an Error .

d: Put a moonpeak server on the internet over HTTPS.
x: Hosts need a public HTTPS URL. The simplest setup is a VPS with Node and a reverse proxy. Node on a server Keep it running with systemd, pm2 or a container. A minimal systemd unit: HTTPS with nginx Get a certificate with certbot nginx d your domain . Add limit_req on /mcp if the server is public. Serverless and edge Mount createHandler from moonpeak/server Fetch API on Workers, Deno Deploy, Bun or a Next.js route; see Production server . The handler is stateless, so it scales horizontally without sticky sessions. After deploying Then add https://your domain/mcp in Claude Connectors or ChatGPT Developer mode → Create app . The moonpeak demo at https://moonpeak ai.com/mcp is deployed exactly this way.

d: Protecting a moonpeak server and testing protected servers.
x: moonpeak's server has no built in auth: put it behind the auth your platform already uses. Protecting your server Mount the handler behind a middleware that checks the request before it reaches /mcp : For per user access in Claude and ChatGPT, implement OAuth 2.1 as described in the MCP authorization spec protected resource metadata plus an authorization server ; hosts run the user through the login flow when they add your connector. Handlers can then read the verified user from the request in your middleware. Testing protected servers The inspector adds headers server side in its proxy, so the token is never exposed to the page.

d: Shapes that work well for MCP Apps.
h: Text tool next to a UI tool
Summary for the model, data for the View
x: Detail card One result, rendered richly, with buttons that call the same tool again with new arguments. Example: moon . Carousel A horizontal list of cards for browsing. Load more pages with useCallTool and keep them in useAppState with share: true , so the model knows which card the user picked. Example: calendar . Review and confirm The model proposes an action, the user approves it in the View, and an app only tool performs it. The model cannot skip the click. Example: review . Text tool next to a UI tool Offer a text only tool for quick answers and a UI tool for exploring. Describe both clearly and add eval cases that check the model picks the right one. Summary for the model, data for the View Return a short content summary and the full data in structuredContent see Tool results , so long lists don't fill the model's context. Keep the chat moving After an important action, either post a message useSendMessage when the model should respond, or update model context useUpdateModelContext when it only needs to know.
